rows.what_the_ink_shows: The top box plainly has Ext^{1-i}, not Ext^{i-1} (crops/43_scan114_L932_top_box.png). In the final sequence, the left inner cohomology degree is 1-i and the right inner degree is -i, as enlarged separately in crops/43_scan114_L932_sequence_left.png and crops/43_scan114_L932_sequence_right.png. The middle degree is i followed by a horizontal sign with a conspicuous short upright attached near its right side, then 1 (crops/43_scan114_L932_sequence_middle.png). That upright favors i+1, but a hooked or retouched minus cannot be excluded from these strokes. The existing certain i-1 is therefore replaced with an in-place i+1|i-1 uncertainty. The complete final sequence is retained in crops/43_scan114_L932_final_sequence.png; there is no terminal arrow to 0 written after its Hom term. Later boxed degrees and the overwritten spectral-sequence degree retain their existing uncertainty markup.
rows.note: This row combines an ink-supported uncertainty edit with mathematical corrections that must remain in the note. Keep the clearly written top exponent 1-i and the clearly written final side degrees 1-i and -i. Under the proposed convention H^j(K,DG)=Ext^{j-1}(R\Gamma(G),Q/Z), the displayed two side degrees correspond to a middle H^{i+1} after setting j=i+1. That consistency supports the question but does not settle the sign paleographically; the added upright in the ink is the reason for reopening the certain i-1 reading. Do not normalize the top exponent, replace f_*G by a derived expression, or append the unwritten terminal zero. The later duality box, shift box, spectral box, and other same-page degree comparisons were inspected; their pre-existing uncertainties are preserved. The packet sweep is prior model evidence, not a claimed personal human check.
